G4A_AGES_001.questionText: Asha is 9 years old now. How old will she be after 6 years?
hints: As the years pass, a person's age goes up by the same number of years.
Add the 6 years to Asha's age now.
Example: Raju is 7 now. After 5 years he will be 7 + 5 = 12 years old.

stepByStep.text: Asha is 9 now.
After 6 years her age goes up by 6: 9 + 6 = 15.
So Asha will be 15 years old.

misconceptions.A: 3 is 9 − 6, her age 6 years ago. The word after means going forward in time, so add.
misconceptions.B: 54 is 9 × 6. Each year adds just 1 to her age, so add 6.
misconceptions.D: 14 is one short. Count on 6 from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15.

G4A_AGES_002.questionText: Meera is 10 years old and her father is 38 years old. How many years older than Meera is her father?
hints: The words how many years older ask for the gap between the two ages.
Subtract Meera's age from her father's age.
Example: a boy is 8 and his mother is 33. She is 33 − 8 = 25 years older.

stepByStep.text: Her father is 38 and Meera is 10.
So her father is 28 years older.

misconceptions.A: 48 is 38 + 10. To find how much older, subtract.
misconceptions.B: 18 takes away one ten too many. 38 − 10 = 28.
misconceptions.C: 38 is the father's age. The question asks how much older he is than Meera.

G4A_AGES_003.questionText: Tina is 8 years old. Her mother is 4 times as old as Tina. How old is her mother?
hints: The words times as old tell you to multiply.
Multiply Tina's age by 4.
Example: Sunil is 6 and his father is 5 times as old, so his father is 6 × 5 = 30.

stepByStep.text: Tina is 8.
Her mother is 4 times as old: 8 × 4 = 32.
So her mother is 32 years old.

misconceptions.B: 12 is 8 + 4. The words 4 times as old mean multiply by 4.
misconceptions.C: 2 is 8 ÷ 4. Her mother is older than Tina, so multiply.

G4A_AGES_004.questionText: Four years ago, Zoya was 6 years old. How old is she now?
hints: The words years ago take you into the past. Coming back to today, the age goes up.
She was 6 then, and 4 years have passed since. Add.
Example: three years ago Kabir was 9, so now he is 9 + 3 = 12.

stepByStep.text: Four years ago Zoya was 6.
Since then 4 years have passed: 6 + 4 = 10.
So Zoya is 10 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 2 is 6 − 4. She was 6 in the past, so today she is older, not younger.
misconceptions.C: 24 is 6 × 4. Each year adds 1 to her age, so add 4.
misconceptions.D: 6 was her age four years ago. Add the 4 years that have passed.

G4A_AGES_005.questionText: Dev was born in the year 2015. How old was he on his birthday in 2024?
hints: Age on a birthday is the number of years from the birth year to that year.
Subtract the birth year from 2024.
Example: someone born in 2010 turns 2021 − 2010 = 11 on the birthday in 2021.

stepByStep.text: Dev was born in 2015.
So Dev was 9 years old on his birthday in 2024.

misconceptions.A: 10 counts both 2015 and 2024. In 2015 he was just born, so count the steps between the years: 9.
misconceptions.B: 8 is one short. From 2015 to 2024 is 9 years.
misconceptions.D: 19 has an extra ten. 2015 to 2025 would be 10 years, so 2015 to 2024 is 9.

G4A_AGES_006.questionText: Rohan's father is 36 years old. Rohan is one-third as old as his father. How old is Rohan?
hints: One-third as old means the age is split into 3 equal parts and you take one of them.
Divide the father's age by 3.
Example: a mother is 40 and her son is one-quarter as old, so the son is 40 ÷ 4 = 10.

stepByStep.text: His father is 36.
One-third of 36 is 36 ÷ 3 = 12.
So Rohan is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 33 is 36 − 3. One-third means divide by 3.
misconceptions.B: 108 is 36 × 3. Rohan is younger than his father, so divide.
misconceptions.C: 18 is half of 36. One-third means 3 equal parts: 36 ÷ 3.

G4A_AGES_007.questionText: Anil is 3 years older than his brother Sunil today. How many years older than Sunil will Anil be after 10 years?
hints: Think about what happens to both brothers as the years go by. Do they grow older at the same pace?
Try it with ages you choose: say Sunil is 5 and Anil is 8. Find both ages after 10 years.
Example: Rita is 4 years older than Gita. If Gita is 6 and Rita is 10, then after 5 years they are 11 and 15, and Rita is still 15 − 11 = 4 years older.

stepByStep.text: Suppose Sunil is 5, so Anil is 8.
After 10 years Sunil is 15 and Anil is 18.
18 − 15 = 3. Both grow older by the same amount, so the gap stays the same.
So Anil will still be 3 years older.

misconceptions.A: Right! Both brothers grow 10 years older, so the gap stays 3.
misconceptions.B: 13 is 3 + 10. Sunil also grows 10 years older, so the gap does not grow.
misconceptions.C: 7 is 10 − 3. The gap between two people's ages never changes.
misconceptions.D: 30 is 3 × 10. The gap stays the same every year.

G4A_AGES_008.questionText: Ravi is 12 years old now. In how many years will he be 20 years old?
hints: You know the age now and the age later. The number of years in between is the gap.
Subtract Ravi's age now from 20.
Example: Simran is 9 now. She will be 15 in 15 − 9 = 6 years.

stepByStep.text: Ravi is 12 now and will be 20 later.
So Ravi will be 20 in 8 years.

misconceptions.A: 32 is 20 + 12. The question asks for the years in between, so subtract.
misconceptions.C: 7 is one short: 12 + 7 = 19. One more year is needed.
misconceptions.D: 9 is one too many: 12 + 9 = 21. Count on from 12 to 20.

G4A_AGES_009.questionText: Amit is 3 years older than Bina. Bina is 2 years older than Chirag. Chirag is 7 years old. How old is Amit?
hints: Start from the person whose age you know and work along the chain, one person at a time.
Chirag is 7 and Bina is 2 years older. Find Bina's age first.
Example: Pari is 4 years older than Qasim, Qasim is 1 year older than Ria, and Ria is 6. Then Qasim is 7 and Pari is 7 + 4 = 11.

stepByStep.text: Bina is 2 years older than Chirag: 7 + 2 = 9.
Amit is 3 years older than Bina: 9 + 3 = 12.
So Amit is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 9 is Bina's age. Amit is 3 years older than Bina.
misconceptions.B: 10 is 7 + 3, which skips Bina. Amit is 3 years older than Bina, and Bina is 9.
misconceptions.C: Right! Chirag is 7, Bina is 9 and Amit is 12.
misconceptions.D: 2 comes from subtracting both gaps. Amit is the oldest of the three, so add.

G4A_AGES_010.questionText: Farhan is 11 years old. His sister Rehana is 3 years younger than him. How old was Rehana 2 years ago?
hints: Find the sister's age now first. Then go back in time.
Rehana is 3 years younger than Farhan: 11 − 3.
Example: Mohan is 16 and his sister is 2 years younger, so she is 14. Five years ago she was 14 − 5 = 9.

stepByStep.text: Rehana's age now: 11 − 3 = 8.
Two years ago she was 2 years younger: 8 − 2 = 6.
So Rehana was 6 years old.

misconceptions.A: 8 is Rehana's age now. The question asks about 2 years ago.
misconceptions.B: 12 comes from adding the 3 years. Rehana is younger than Farhan, so subtract.
misconceptions.C: 10 is 8 + 2, her age two years from now. The word ago means going back.
misconceptions.D: Yes! She is 8 now, so two years ago she was 6.

G4A_AGES_011.questionText: Diya is 7 years old and her mother is 35 years old. After 7 years, how many times as old as Diya will her mother be?
hints: Both people grow older. Find both new ages first, then compare them by dividing.
After 7 years, Diya will be 7 + 7 and her mother will be 35 + 7.
Example: a boy is 4 and his father is 34. After 2 years they are 6 and 36, and 36 ÷ 6 = 6, so the father is 6 times as old.

stepByStep.text: After 7 years Diya will be 7 + 7 = 14.
Her mother will be 35 + 7 = 42.
So her mother will be 3 times as old as Diya.

misconceptions.A: Right! 42 is 3 times 14.
misconceptions.B: 5 times is true today, since 35 ÷ 7 = 5. After 7 years both ages change.
misconceptions.C: Check the dividing: 14 × 4 = 56, which is more than 42. Try 14 × 3.
misconceptions.D: 28 is the gap between their ages, which never changes. The words how many times ask you to divide.

G4A_AGES_012.questionText: The sum of the ages of Anu and her mother is 44 years. Anu is 8 years old. How old was her mother when Anu was born?
hints: Find the mother's age now. Then go back to the year Anu was born.
Mother's age now: 44 − 8.
Example: a boy of 5 and his father have ages adding up to 40. The father is 35 now, and when the boy was born, 5 years ago, he was 35 − 5 = 30.

stepByStep.text: Mother's age now: 44 − 8 = 36.
Anu was born 8 years ago.
Her mother was then 36 − 8 = 28.
So her mother was 28 years old when Anu was born.

misconceptions.A: 36 is her mother's age now. Anu was born 8 years ago, so go back 8 years.
misconceptions.B: Yes! She is 36 now, so she was 28 when Anu was born.
misconceptions.C: 44 is the two ages together. Take away Anu's 8 to get her mother's age, then go back 8 years.
misconceptions.D: 52 is 44 + 8. Take Anu's age away from the sum instead.

G4A_AGES_013.questionText: The ages of two sisters add up to 20 years. One sister is 4 years older than the other. How old is the older sister?
hints: You know the sum and the difference of two ages. Take away the extra years and the rest splits equally.
Take the extra 4 years away from 20. What is left is twice the younger sister's age.
Example: two ages add up to 34 and differ by 6. 34 − 6 = 28, and half of 28 is 14, so the younger is 14 and the older is 14 + 6 = 20.

stepByStep.text: Take away the extra years: 20 − 4 = 16.
Half of 16 is 8, so the younger sister is 8.
The older sister is 8 + 4 = 12.
So the older sister is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 8 is the younger sister's age. Add 4 for the older sister.
misconceptions.B: 16 is 20 − 4. It still has to be split between the two sisters.
misconceptions.C: Right! The sisters are 8 and 12: together 20, and 4 apart.
misconceptions.D: 10 is half of 20, which would make the sisters the same age. One is 4 years older.

G4A_AGES_014.questionText: A father is 3 times as old as his son. Their ages add up to 48 years. How old is the son?
hints: Think of the son's age as 1 part. Then the father's age is a number of the same parts, and you can count all the parts in the sum.
The son is 1 part and the father is 3 parts. That makes 4 parts adding up to 48.
Example: a mother is 4 times as old as her daughter and their ages add up to 40. That is 5 parts, so the daughter is 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

stepByStep.text: The son is 1 part and the father is 3 parts, so together they are 4 parts.
4 parts are 48, so one part is 48 ÷ 4 = 12.
So the son is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 16 is 48 ÷ 3. Count the son's own part too: there are 4 parts in all.
misconceptions.B: 36 is the father's age. The son is one part: 12.
misconceptions.C: 24 is half of 48, which would make them the same age. The father has 3 parts and the son has 1.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The son is 12 and the father is 36: together 48.

G4A_AGES_015.questionText: Three years ago, Kiran was 9 years old. How old will she be 4 years from now?
hints: Move along the timeline in two jumps: from the past to today, then from today to the future.
First find Kiran's age today: 9 + 3.
Example: four years ago Jai was 5, so he is 9 now. Two years from now he will be 9 + 2 = 11.

stepByStep.text: Kiran's age today: 9 + 3 = 12.
Four years from now: 12 + 4 = 16.
So Kiran will be 16 years old.

misconceptions.A: Right! She was 9 then, is 12 now, and will be 16 four years from now.
misconceptions.B: 13 is 9 + 4, which skips the 3 years that have already passed. Find her age today first.
misconceptions.C: 10 takes away 3 instead of adding. She was 9 in the past, so today she is 12.
misconceptions.D: 12 is Kiran's age today. Go 4 more years ahead.

G4A_AGES_016.questionText: The ages of Geeta and Hari add up to 25 years now. What did their ages add up to 3 years ago?
hints: Going back in time changes the age of each person, not just one. Count how many people are in the sum.
Three years ago Geeta was 3 years younger, and so was Hari. How much smaller was the sum?
Example: two friends' ages add up to 30. Five years ago each was 5 years younger, so the sum was 30 − 5 − 5 = 20.

stepByStep.text: Three years ago Geeta was 3 years younger and Hari was 3 years younger.
Together that is 3 + 3 = 6 years less.
25 − 6 = 19, so their ages added up to 19 years.

misconceptions.A: 22 takes away 3 only once. Both Geeta and Hari were 3 years younger.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Each was 3 years younger, so the sum was 6 less: 19.
misconceptions.C: 28 adds 3. The word ago goes back in time, so the ages were smaller.
misconceptions.D: 31 adds 6. The word ago goes back in time, so take 6 away instead.

G4A_AGES_017.questionText: Jay's grandfather is 72 years old. Jay's father is half as old as the grandfather. Jay is one-quarter as old as his father. How old is Jay?
hints: Work down the family one step at a time, using each age to find the next.
Find the father's age first: half of 72.
Example: a grandmother is 60, the mother is half as old, so 30, and the child is one-fifth as old as the mother: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

stepByStep.text: Father's age: 72 ÷ 2 = 36.
Jay's age is one-quarter of 36: 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
So Jay is 9 years old.

misconceptions.A: 18 is one-quarter of the grandfather's age. Jay's age is one-quarter of his father's age, 36.
misconceptions.B: 36 is the father's age. Now take one-quarter of it.
misconceptions.C: Right! The father is 36, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
misconceptions.D: 12 is 36 ÷ 3. One-quarter means 4 equal parts: 36 ÷ 4.

G4A_AGES_018.questionText: Varun is 9 years old. His father is 27 years older than him. How old will his father be when Varun is 15?
hints: The gap between two people's ages stays the same for ever. Use it at the later time.
When Varun is 15, his father will still be 27 years older than him.
Example: Nita is 6 and her mother is 24 years older. When Nita is 10, her mother will be 10 + 24 = 34.

stepByStep.text: The father is always 27 years older than Varun.
When Varun is 15, his father will be 15 + 27 = 42.
So his father will be 42 years old.

misconceptions.A: 36 is the father's age now, 9 + 27. By the time Varun is 15, six more years have passed.
misconceptions.B: 33 is 27 + 6. The 27 is the gap, not the father's age: his age now is 36.
misconceptions.C: 51 is 36 + 15. Only 6 years pass between Varun being 9 and 15, so add 6 to 36.

G4A_AGES_019.questionText: Rahul is 10 years old and his father is 40 years old. After how many years will the father be 3 times as old as Rahul?
hints: Both ages go up together. Try a number of years, find both new ages, and check whether one is 3 times the other.
Try each choice. After 10 years they would be 20 and 50. Is 50 equal to 3 times 20?
Example: a girl is 6 and her mother is 30. After 2 years they are 8 and 32, and 32 is 4 times 8, so after 2 years the mother is 4 times as old.

stepByStep.text: After 5 years Rahul will be 10 + 5 = 15.
His father will be 40 + 5 = 45.
45 is 3 times 15, so the father is then 3 times as old.
So it happens after 5 years.

misconceptions.A: Right! After 5 years they are 15 and 45, and 45 is 3 times 15.
misconceptions.B: After 10 years they are 20 and 50, but 3 times 20 is 60. Try fewer years.
misconceptions.C: After 15 years they are 25 and 55, but 3 times 25 is 75. Try fewer years.
misconceptions.D: After 20 years they are 30 and 60, and 60 is only 2 times 30. Try fewer years.

G4A_AGES_020.questionText: Ali is 14 years old and his sister Sara is 8 years old. How old was Ali when Sara was exactly half his age?
hints: The gap between their ages never changes. When one person is half the other's age, the younger one's age equals the gap.
Find the gap: 14 − 8. When Sara's age was equal to this gap, Ali was twice as old as her.
Example: Ravi is 15 and Mala is 11, a gap of 4. When Mala was 4, Ravi was 4 + 4 = 8, exactly double.

stepByStep.text: Ali is always 14 − 8 = 6 years older than Sara.
Sara is half Ali's age when her age equals the gap, so Sara was 6.
Ali was then 6 + 6 = 12.
So Ali was 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 7 is half of Ali's age today. When Ali was 7, Sara was only 1. Use the gap of 6 years.
misconceptions.B: Yes! When Ali was 12, Sara was 6, exactly half.
misconceptions.C: 6 was Sara's age at that time. The question asks for Ali's age.
misconceptions.D: When Ali was 10, Sara was 4, and half of 10 is 5. Go to the time when Sara was 6.

G4A_AGES_021.questionText: Five years ago, a mother was 7 times as old as her daughter. The mother is 33 years old now. How old is the daughter now?
hints: Go back to the time the clue talks about, work out the ages then, and return to today.
Find the mother's age five years ago: 33 − 5.
Example: four years ago a father was 6 times as old as his son. The father is 40 now, so he was 36 then and the son was 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Today the son is 6 + 4 = 10.

stepByStep.text: Five years ago the mother was 33 − 5 = 28.
The daughter was then 28 ÷ 7 = 4.
Today the daughter is 4 + 5 = 9.
So the daughter is 9 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 4 was the daughter's age five years ago. Add the 5 years to come back to today.
misconceptions.B: 14 adds the 5 years twice. From 4, add 5 just once.
misconceptions.C: Right! She was 4 then, so she is 9 now.
misconceptions.D: 28 was the mother's age five years ago. Divide by 7 for the daughter's age then, and come back to today.

G4A_AGES_022.questionText: Aman is twice as old as Bhavna. Four years ago, Aman was three times as old as Bhavna was then. How old is Bhavna now?
hints: Two clues must both be true. Try an age, use the first clue to get the other age, then test the second clue.
Try a choice: if Bhavna is 12, Aman is 24. Four years ago they were 8 and 20. Is 20 three times 8?
Example: Meena is twice as old as Nitu, and five years ago she was three times as old. Try Nitu 10 and Meena 20: five years ago they were 5 and 15, and 15 is 3 times 5. So Nitu is 10.

stepByStep.text: Try Bhavna as 8: then Aman is 2 × 8 = 16.
Four years ago Bhavna was 8 − 4 = 4 and Aman was 16 − 4 = 12.
12 is 3 times 4, so both clues fit.
So Bhavna is 8 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 16 is Aman's age. The question asks for Bhavna, who is half as old.
misconceptions.B: 4 was Bhavna's age four years ago. Add the 4 years to come back to today.
misconceptions.C: If Bhavna were 12, Aman would be 24, and four years ago they would be 8 and 20. But 3 times 8 is 24, not 20.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Bhavna is 8 and Aman is 16 now; four years ago they were 4 and 12, and 12 is 3 times 4.

G4A_AGES_023.questionText: A grandfather is 9 times as old as his grandson. Their ages add up to 70 years. How old will the grandfather be when the grandson is 10 years old?
hints: Use parts to find both ages now. Then move both people forward by the same number of years.
The grandson is 1 part and the grandfather is 9 parts, so 10 parts make 70. Find one part.
Example: a father is 5 times as old as his daughter and their ages add up to 36. Six parts make 36, so she is 6 and he is 30. When she is 8, two years later, he will be 30 + 2 = 32.

stepByStep.text: The grandson is 1 part and the grandfather is 9 parts. 10 parts are 70, so one part is 70 ÷ 10 = 7.
The grandson is 7 and the grandfather is 9 × 7 = 63.
The grandson will be 10 after 10 − 7 = 3 years.
63 + 3 = 66, so the grandfather will be 66 years old.

misconceptions.A: Right! He is 63 now, and 3 years later he is 66.
misconceptions.B: 63 is the grandfather's age now. The grandson is 7 now, so move 3 years ahead.
misconceptions.C: 73 adds 10 years. The grandson needs only 3 more years to reach 10.
misconceptions.D: 90 is 9 × 10. He is 9 times as old only now; later, both simply grow older by the same number of years.

G4A_AGES_024.questionText: Neel says that in 6 years he will be twice as old as he was 2 years ago. How old is Neel now?
hints: Compare two moments: one in the past and one in the future. Count the years between them.
From 2 years ago to 6 years from now is 2 + 6 = 8 years. In those 8 years his age doubles.
Example: in 5 years Tanu will be twice as old as she was 1 year ago. Those moments are 6 years apart, so she was 6 one year ago, and she is 6 + 1 = 7 now.

stepByStep.text: From 2 years ago to 6 years from now is 2 + 6 = 8 years.
His age doubles in those 8 years, so 2 years ago he was 8.
Now he is 8 + 2 = 10.
Check: in 6 years he will be 16, which is twice 8. So Neel is 10 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 8 was Neel's age 2 years ago. Add 2 to come to today.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Two years ago he was 8, and in 6 years he will be 16, which is twice 8. So he is 10 now.
misconceptions.C: 16 will be Neel's age in 6 years. Come back 6 years to today.
misconceptions.D: If Neel were 14, he would be 20 in 6 years, but twice his age 2 years ago would be 24. Try a smaller age.

G4A_AGES_025.questionText: Three sisters were born 2 years apart, one after another. Their ages add up to 27 years. How old is the youngest sister?
hints: When ages are equally spaced, the middle one is the equal share. Find the middle age first.
Share 27 equally among the three sisters to find the middle sister's age: 27 ÷ 3.
Example: three brothers born 3 years apart have ages adding up to 45. The middle one is 45 ÷ 3 = 15, so the youngest is 15 − 3 = 12.

stepByStep.text: The middle sister's age is 27 ÷ 3 = 9.
The youngest is 2 years younger: 9 − 2 = 7.
So the youngest sister is 7 years old.

misconceptions.A: 9 is the middle sister's age. The youngest is 2 years younger.
misconceptions.B: 11 is the oldest sister's age. The question asks for the youngest.
misconceptions.C: Right! The sisters are 7, 9 and 11, which add up to 27.
misconceptions.D: 5 takes away 2 twice from the middle age. The youngest is just 2 years younger than the middle sister.

G4A_AGES_026.questionText: Five years ago, a family had 4 members and their average age was 19 years. Since then a baby has been born, and no one else has joined or left the family. Today the average age of the 5 members is 20 years. How old is the baby?
hints: Averages hide totals. Find the total of the ages five years ago, then think about how each person has changed since.
Five years ago the 4 members had a total age of 4 × 19 = 76 years. Each of them is 5 years older now. What is their total today?
A similar one: 3 people averaged 20 two years ago, a total of 60. Now they total 60 + 6 = 66. With a new baby the 4 people average 17, a total of 68, so the baby is 68 − 66 = 2 years old.

stepByStep.text: Find the total age of the 4 members five years ago.
Each of the 4 is now 5 years older.
Find the total age of all 5 members today.
The baby's age is the difference.
The baby is 4 years old.

misconceptions.A: 24 is 100 − 76. That compares today's total with the total of five years ago. The four older members have each grown 5 years since then.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The four older members now total 96 years, the family totals 100, so the baby is 4.
misconceptions.C: 1 is the change in the average, from 19 to 20. Work with total ages: 76 then, 96 now for the same four people, and 100 for all five.
misconceptions.D: 19 comes from adding 5 years only once. All 4 members grew 5 years older, which adds 20 years to their total.

G4A_AGES_027.questionText: The ages of a father, a mother and their son add up to 75 years. The son is 3 years old. Five years ago, what did the ages of this family add up to?
hints: Go back 5 years for each person separately. Check that each person had been born by then.
The son is 3 now. Where was he 5 years ago? Find what the father and mother add up to now, without the son.
A similar one: a mother, a father and a 2-year-old girl total 82 now. Four years ago the girl was not born. The parents total 80 now, and 4 years ago they totalled 80 − 8 = 72.

stepByStep.text: The son is 3, so 5 years ago he was not yet born.
Find the parents' total now.
Each parent was 5 years younger then.
Five years ago the family's ages added up to 62 years.

misconceptions.A: 60 takes 5 years off all three people. The son is only 3, so he was not born 5 years ago. Take 5 years off the two parents only.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The parents total 72 now, and 5 years ago they were 10 years less in total, which is 62.
misconceptions.C: 70 takes away 5 just once. Each parent was 5 years younger, and the son's 3 years must come out too.
misconceptions.D: 65 takes 5 years off the two parents but still counts the son's 3 years. He was not born yet, so leave him out.

G4A_AGES_028.questionText: When Meera was born, her mother was 26 years old. Today her mother is exactly 3 times as old as Meera. How old is her mother today?
hints: The gap between two people's ages never changes. Use the gap together with the 'times as old' clue.
The mother is always 26 years older than Meera. If Meera's age is 1 part and her mother's is 3 parts, how many parts is the gap?
A similar one: a father was 30 when his son was born and is now 4 times as old. The gap of 30 is 3 parts, so one part is 10. The son is 10 and the father is 40.

stepByStep.text: The mother is always 26 years older than Meera.
Meera's age is 1 part and her mother's is 3 parts, so the gap is 2 parts.
Find one part, which is Meera's age.
The mother is 3 parts.
Her mother is 39 years old today.

misconceptions.A: 78 is 26 × 3. But 26 was the mother's age long ago, not Meera's age. Use 26 as the gap between their ages.
misconceptions.B: 13 is Meera's age today. The question asks for her mother, who is 3 times as old.
misconceptions.C: 52 is 26 × 2. Check it: Meera would be 52 − 26 = 26, and 52 is not 3 times 26. The gap of 26 is 2 parts.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Meera is 13 and her mother is 39, which is 3 times 13 and 26 more than 13.

G4A_AGES_029.questionText: Anu and Bela are 20 years old together. Bela and Charu are 26 years old together. Anu and Charu are 24 years old together. How old is Charu?
hints: Each child appears in two of the three totals. Think about what you get if you add all three totals.
Add 20, 26 and 24. Every child has been counted twice in this sum, so what do the three ages add up to?
A similar one: P and Q total 10, Q and R total 14, P and R total 12. The sum 36 counts everyone twice, so the three total 18. Then R is 18 − 10 = 8.

stepByStep.text: Add the three totals. Each child is counted twice.
Halve to get the total of the three ages.
Anu and Bela make 20 of this, so the rest is Charu.
Charu is 15 years old.

misconceptions.A: 11 is Bela's age. Take away Anu and Bela's total of 20 from 35 to leave Charu.
misconceptions.B: 9 is Anu's age. Take away Anu and Bela's total of 20 from 35 to leave Charu.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The three ages total 35, and without Anu and Bela's 20 that leaves 15 for Charu.
misconceptions.D: 35 is the three ages added together. Take away Anu and Bela's total to find Charu's age.

G4A_AGES_030.questionText: A father is 40 years old. His three children are 4, 6 and 8 years old. After how many years will the father's age be equal to the sum of the ages of his three children?
hints: Each year the father grows 1 year older, but the three children together grow 3 years older. Watch how fast the gap closes.
The children's ages add up to 18 now, so the gap is 40 − 18 = 22. How much smaller does this gap get every year?
A similar one: a mother is 30 and her two children are 5 and 7, a gap of 18. Each year the mother gains 1 and the children gain 2, so the gap closes by 1 a year and takes 18 years.

stepByStep.text: Add the children's ages now.
Find the gap to the father's age.
Each year the children gain 3 years in total and the father gains 1, so the gap closes by 2 years each year.
Find how long the gap takes to close.
Check: the father will be 51 and the children 15, 17 and 19, which add up to 51.
It will happen after 11 years.

misconceptions.A: Yes! In 11 years the father is 51 and the children are 15, 17 and 19, which also add up to 51.
misconceptions.B: 22 is the gap today. The gap does not close by 1 a year: the children gain 3 years in total while the father gains 1, so it closes by 2 a year.
misconceptions.C: 7 comes from dividing the gap by 3. The father also grows older each year, so the gap closes by only 2 years each year.
misconceptions.D: 18 is the sum of the children's ages now. Find how far that is from 40 and how quickly the gap closes.

G4A_AGES_031.questionText: A mother was 28 years old when her twin daughters were born. Today the ages of the mother and the two twins add up to 64 years. How old is each twin?
hints: Since the twins were born, three people have been growing older, not two. Count the mother too.
When the twins were born the three ages added up to 28. Every year after that, how much does the total grow?
A similar one: a father was 30 when his twin sons were born, and today the three ages total 60. The total has grown by 30, at 3 years each year, so 10 years have passed and each twin is 10.

stepByStep.text: At the birth of the twins the three ages added up to 28.
Find how much the total has grown since then.
Each year all three people grow a year older, so the total grows by 3.
Check: the mother is 40 and the twins are 12 and 12.
Each twin is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 18 shares the extra 36 years between the two twins only. The mother has also grown older, so 36 is shared among three people.
misconceptions.B: 36 is how much the total of the ages has grown. Three people have each grown by the same number of years, so divide by 3.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 12 years have passed: the mother is 40 and each twin is 12, and 40 + 12 + 12 = 64.
misconceptions.D: 9 comes from dividing 36 by 4. Only three people are growing older: the mother and the two twins.

G4A_AGES_032.questionText: A father's age and his son's age are written with the same two digits, but in the opposite order. The father is 27 years older than his son, and the son is a teenager (13 to 19 years old). How old is the father?
hints: Test the possible ages one by one. For each age, swap the digits and check both clues.
The son is between 13 and 19. Start with 13: the father would be 31, and 31 − 13 = 18. That gap is too small, so try the next age.
A similar one: a mother and daughter have ages with swapped digits, 36 years apart, and the daughter is under 20. Try 15 and 51: the gap is 36, so the mother is 51.

stepByStep.text: List the son's possible ages, 13 to 19, with the digits swapped for the father: 31, 41, 51, 61, 71, 81, 91.
Find the gap for each pair: 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72.
Only 14 and 41 have a gap of 27.
The father is 41 years old.

misconceptions.A: 52 and 25 are 27 apart and share digits, but then the son would be 25, which is not a teenager. Test the ages from 13 to 19.
misconceptions.B: 63 and 36 are 27 apart, but a son of 36 is not a teenager. Test the ages from 13 to 19.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The son is 14, the father is 41, and 41 − 14 = 27.
misconceptions.D: 74 and 47 are 27 apart, but a son of 47 is not a teenager. Test the ages from 13 to 19.

G4A_AGES_033.questionText: Asha is 8 years old. She tells her older sister Bina, 'When I am as old as you are now, you will be 20 years old.' How old is Bina now?
hints: The gap between the sisters stays the same. From 8 to Bina's age is one gap, and from Bina's age to 20 is the same gap again.
Asha needs some years to reach Bina's age. In those same years Bina grows to 20. So Bina's age is exactly in the middle of two numbers. Which two?
A similar one: Ravi is 6 and says that when he is as old as Sam is now, Sam will be 16. Sam's age is halfway between 6 and 16, which is 11. Check: in 5 years Ravi is 11 and Sam is 16.

stepByStep.text: Asha needs a certain number of years to reach Bina's age. In those same years Bina reaches 20.
So from 8 to Bina's age and from Bina's age to 20 are two equal steps. Find the two steps together.
Each step is half of that.
Bina's age is one step above 8.
Check: in 6 years Asha is 14 and Bina is 20.
Bina is 14 years old now.

misconceptions.A: Yes! Bina is 6 years older. In 6 years Asha will be 14, Bina's age now, and Bina will be 20.
misconceptions.B: 12 is 20 − 8, which is two gaps, not Bina's age. Bina is halfway between 8 and 20.
misconceptions.C: If Bina were 16, Asha would need 8 years to reach 16, and Bina would then be 24, not 20. Try the age halfway between 8 and 20.
misconceptions.D: 28 is 20 + 8. Bina will be 20 in the future, so she must be younger than 20 now.

G4A_AGES_034.questionText: Ravi's age this year is a multiple of 3. Last year his age was a multiple of 4. Next year his age will be a multiple of 5. Ravi is less than 60 years old. How old is he this year?
hints: Three clues must all be true together. List the ages that fit one clue, then test them against the others.
Start with next year's age, which ends in 0 or 5. So this year's age ends in 9 or 4. Which of those are multiples of 3?
A similar one: an age is a multiple of 4, and one year later it is a multiple of 5, and it is under 20. Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16. Adding 1 gives 5, 9, 13, 17, and only 5 fits. So the age is 4.

stepByStep.text: Next year's age is a multiple of 5, so it ends in 0 or 5. This year's age ends in 9 or 4.
Ages under 60 that end in 9 or 4 and are multiples of 3 are 9, 24, 39 and 54.
Last year's ages would be 8, 23, 38 and 53. Only 8 is a multiple of 4.
Ravi is 9 years old this year.

misconceptions.A: 21 is a multiple of 3 and last year's 20 is a multiple of 4. But next year's 22 is not a multiple of 5. All three clues must fit.
misconceptions.B: 24 is a multiple of 3 and next year's 25 is a multiple of 5. But last year's 23 is not a multiple of 4. All three clues must fit.
misconceptions.C: 39 is a multiple of 3 and next year's 40 is a multiple of 5. But last year's 38 is not a multiple of 4. All three clues must fit.
misconceptions.D: Yes! 9 is a multiple of 3, last year's 8 is a multiple of 4, and next year's 10 is a multiple of 5.

G4A_AGES_035.questionText: Ritu and her two brothers are all more than 4 years old. Five years from now, their three ages will add up to 50 years. What did their three ages add up to 2 years ago?
hints: When time moves, every person's age moves. Count how many people there are and how many years you are moving.
From 5 years in the future back to today, each of the 3 children is 5 years younger. Find what the ages add up to today first.
A similar one: in 4 years, two sisters' ages will total 30. Today they total 30 − 8 = 22. Three years ago they totalled 22 − 6 = 16.

stepByStep.text: Go back from 5 years ahead to today. Each of the 3 children is 5 years younger.
Go back 2 more years. Each of the 3 children is 2 years younger.
Two years ago their ages added up to 29 years.

misconceptions.A: 43 takes away 5 + 2 = 7 just once. There are three children, and each one's age changes by 7 years, so the total changes by 21.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Going back 7 years for each of 3 children takes 21 off the total, and 50 − 21 = 29.
misconceptions.C: 35 is what their ages add up to today. The question asks about 2 years ago, so go back 2 more years for each child.
misconceptions.D: 41 goes back 5 years but then forward 2 years. Two years ago is further back, so subtract again.

G4A_AGES_036.questionText: A mother is 5 times as old as her daughter. In 6 years, their ages will add up to 60 years. How old is the daughter now?
hints: The 'times as old' clue is about today, but the total is about the future. Bring the total back to today first.
In 6 years both the mother and the daughter will be 6 years older. Take both of those away from 60 to get today's total.
A similar one: a father is 4 times as old as his son, and in 5 years their ages will total 60. Today they total 60 − 10 = 50, which is 5 parts, so the son is 10 and the father is 40.

stepByStep.text: Bring the total back to today. Two people are each 6 years younger.
Today the daughter is 1 part and the mother is 5 parts.
Find one part.
Check: 8 and 40 now, 14 and 46 in 6 years.
The daughter is 8 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 10 is 60 ÷ 6, but 60 is the total in 6 years' time. The mother is 5 times as old today, so find today's total first.
misconceptions.B: 9 comes from taking 6 off the total only once. Both the mother and the daughter will be 6 years older, so take off 12.
misconceptions.C: 40 is the mother's age now. The question asks for the daughter, who is one of the 6 parts.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Today they total 48: the daughter is 8 and the mother is 40. In 6 years they are 14 and 46, which make 60.

G4A_AGES_037.questionText: The ages of two cousins multiply to give 84. The older cousin is 5 years older than the younger one. What do their two ages add up to?
hints: List the pairs of numbers that multiply to give 84. Then look for the pair with the right gap.
Some pairs are 2 and 42, 3 and 28, 4 and 21. Keep going and find the gap between the two numbers in each pair.
A similar one: two ages multiply to 40 and are 3 apart. The pairs are 1 and 40, 2 and 20, 4 and 10, 5 and 8. Only 5 and 8 are 3 apart, and they add up to 13.

stepByStep.text: List the pairs that multiply to 84: 1 and 84, 2 and 42, 3 and 28, 4 and 21, 6 and 14, 7 and 12.
Find the gap in each pair: 83, 40, 25, 17, 8 and 5.
Only 7 and 12 are 5 apart.
Add the two ages.
Their ages add up to 19 years.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The cousins are 7 and 12: these multiply to 84, are 5 apart, and add up to 19.
misconceptions.B: 20 is 6 + 14. These multiply to 84, but they are 8 apart, not 5. Keep testing the pairs.
misconceptions.C: 25 is 4 + 21. These multiply to 84, but they are 17 apart, not 5. Keep testing the pairs.
misconceptions.D: 31 is 3 + 28. These multiply to 84, but they are 25 apart, not 5. Keep testing the pairs.

G4A_AGES_038.questionText: Kabir's age in months is the same number as his grandfather's age in years. Their ages add up to 78 years. How old is Kabir?
hints: Change both ages to the same unit. Think about how many months make one year.
If Kabir is 1 year old he is 12 months old, so his grandfather would be 12 years old. The grandfather's age is always how many times Kabir's age?

A similar one: a girl's age in months equals her aunt's age in years, and together they are 39 years. The aunt is 12 times as old, so there are 13 parts. One part is 3, so the girl is 3 and the aunt is 36.

stepByStep.text: A year has 12 months, so Kabir's age in months is 12 times his age in years. His grandfather is 12 times as old as Kabir.
Kabir is 1 part and his grandfather is 12 parts.
Find one part.
Check: Kabir is 6 years, which is 72 months, and his grandfather is 72 years.
Kabir is 6 years old.

misconceptions.A: 12 is the number of months in a year. It tells you the grandfather is 12 times as old as Kabir. Share 78 into 13 parts.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Kabir is 6 years, or 72 months, old. His grandfather is 72, and 6 + 72 = 78.
misconceptions.C: 39 is half of 78, but the two ages are not equal. The grandfather is 12 times as old as Kabir.
misconceptions.D: 72 is the grandfather's age in years. Kabir is 72 months old, so change that into years.

G4A_AGES_039.questionText: Tara's age and her uncle's age are in the ratio 2 : 5. Six years ago, their ages were in the ratio 1 : 4. How old is her uncle now?
hints: Ages in the ratio 2 : 5 could be 2 and 5, 4 and 10, 6 and 15, and so on. Test these pairs against the clue about six years ago.
Both people must be older than 6. Try 8 and 20: six years ago they were 2 and 14. Is 14 exactly 4 times 2? If not, try the next pair.

A similar one: ages in the ratio 1 : 3 now, and 1 : 5 four years ago. Try 6 and 18: four years ago they were 2 and 14, which is 1 : 7. Try 8 and 24: four years ago they were 4 and 20, which is 1 : 5. So the ages are 8 and 24.

stepByStep.text: List pairs in the ratio 2 : 5 with both ages above 6: 8 and 20, 10 and 25, 12 and 30, 14 and 35, 16 and 40.
Take 6 years off each: 2 and 14, 4 and 19, 6 and 24, 8 and 29, 10 and 34.
Look for the pair where the second is 4 times the first. Only 6 and 24 fit.
That pair comes from 12 and 30, so her uncle is 30 years old now.

misconceptions.A: If the uncle is 20, Tara is 8. Six years ago they were 2 and 14, and 14 is 7 times 2, not 4 times. Try an older pair.
misconceptions.B: If the uncle is 25, Tara is 10. Six years ago they were 4 and 19, and 19 is not 4 times 4. Try another pair.
misconceptions.C: Yes! Tara is 12 and her uncle is 30. Six years ago they were 6 and 24, which is 1 : 4.
misconceptions.D: If the uncle is 40, Tara is 16. Six years ago they were 10 and 34, and 34 is not 4 times 10. Try a younger pair.

G4A_ALGEBRA_001.questionText: Meera had ₹p. She bought 3 pencils that cost ₹q each. Which expression shows the money she has left, in rupees?
hints: Money left is the money she had minus the money she spent. Write the money spent as an expression first.
One pencil costs q rupees. Write the cost of 3 pencils using q, then take it away from p.
A similar one: Arun had ₹m and bought 5 erasers at ₹n each. The erasers cost 5n rupees, so he has m − 5n rupees left.

stepByStep.text: One pencil costs q rupees, so 3 pencils cost 3 times q, which is 3q rupees.
Money left = money she had − money she spent.
So the money left is p − 3q rupees.

misconceptions.A: Here the 3 is joined to p. It is the pencil price q that is taken 3 times, not Meera's money.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Three pencils cost 3q, and taking that from p leaves p − 3q.
misconceptions.C: This takes the price away 3 times but also makes her money 3 times as big. Only the price q is multiplied by 3.
misconceptions.D: This takes away the price of one pencil and then the number 3. Three pencils cost 3 times q.

G4A_ALGEBRA_002.questionText: In a cricket match a team scored r runs in the first innings. In the second innings it scored 40 runs fewer. Which expression shows the total runs in both innings?
hints: Write an expression for each innings, then add the two expressions together.
The first innings is r. The second innings is 40 fewer than r. Write that with a minus sign.
A similar one: a shop sold k kites on Monday and 15 more on Tuesday. Tuesday is k + 15, so the total is k + k + 15 = 2k + 15.

stepByStep.text: First innings: r runs.
Second innings: 40 fewer, so r − 40 runs.
Add the two innings: r + r − 40. The two r terms make 2r.
The total is 2r − 40.

misconceptions.A: r − 40 is the score of the second innings only. Add the first innings to it.
misconceptions.B: Here 40 has been taken away twice. Only the second innings is 40 fewer.
misconceptions.C: 2r would be the total if both innings were the same. The second innings is 40 runs fewer.

hints: Only like terms can be put together. Collect the terms with a, and separately the terms with b.
The a terms are 7a and − 2a. The b terms are 3b and b. Remember that b on its own means 1b.
A similar one: 4x + 2y + 3x − y. The x terms give 7x and the y terms give 2y − y = y. The result is 7x + y.

stepByStep.text: Collect the a terms: 7a − 2a = 5a.
Collect the b terms: 3b + b = 4b, because b means 1b.
The a terms and b terms are unlike, so they stay separate.
The simplified expression is 5a + 4b.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 7a − 2a = 5a and 3b + b = 4b.
misconceptions.B: Terms with a and terms with b are unlike, so they cannot be joined into one term. Collect each letter separately.
misconceptions.C: The lone b counts as 1b, so 3b + b is 4b.
misconceptions.D: The sign in front of 2a is minus, so 7a − 2a = 5a.

G4A_ALGEBRA_004.questionText: The odd numbers in order are 1, 3, 5, 7, ... Which expression gives the nth odd number?
hints: A good rule must fit every position, not just the first. Test each expression with n = 1, n = 2 and n = 3.
The 1st odd number is 1, the 2nd is 3 and the 3rd is 5. Compare them with the even numbers 2, 4, 6 in the same positions.
A similar one: the numbers 5, 10, 15, ... are given by 5n. The numbers 4, 9, 14, ... are each one less, so they are given by 5n − 1.

stepByStep.text: The even numbers 2, 4, 6, 8, ... are 2 times their position, so the nth even number is 2n.
Each odd number 1, 3, 5, 7, ... is one less than the even number in the same position.
Check with n = 4: 2 times 4 is 8, and one less is 7, the 4th odd number.
The nth odd number is 2n − 1.

misconceptions.A: n + 2 gives 3 for n = 1, but the 1st odd number is 1. Going up by 2 each time means the rule has 2n in it.
misconceptions.B: 3n − 2 fits n = 1, but for n = 2 it gives 4, which is not odd. Test more than one position.
misconceptions.D: 2n gives 2, 4, 6, which are the even numbers. The odd numbers are one less.

G4A_ALGEBRA_005.questionText: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of (2a + 3) cm each. Its third side is (a − 2) cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
hints: The perimeter is the sum of all three sides. An isosceles triangle has two sides that are the same, so one expression is added twice.
Write the three sides in a row: (2a + 3), (2a + 3) and (a − 2). Collect the a terms first, then the plain numbers.
A similar one: equal sides of (x + 4) cm each and a third side of (x − 1) cm. The x terms give 3x and the numbers give 4 + 4 − 1 = 7. The perimeter is (3x + 7) cm.

stepByStep.text: Add the three sides: (2a + 3) + (2a + 3) + (a − 2).
Collect the a terms: 2a + 2a + a = 5a.
Collect the numbers: 3 + 3 − 2 = 4.
The perimeter is (5a + 4) cm.

misconceptions.A: This adds only one of the equal sides. An isosceles triangle has two sides of (2a + 3) cm.
misconceptions.B: Yes! 5a from the letters and 3 + 3 − 2 = 4 from the numbers.
misconceptions.C: The a terms are right, but the 3 must be counted twice: 3 + 3 − 2 = 4.
misconceptions.D: The third side is a − 2, so 2 is taken away, not added: 3 + 3 − 2 = 4.

G4A_ALGEBRA_006.questionText: A rectangular garden is p metres long and q metres wide. One long side is along a wall, so a fence is put only on the other three sides. What is the length of the fence?
hints: Picture the four sides of the rectangle: two long sides and two short sides. Decide which sides get a fence.
The wall takes the place of one long side of p metres. The fence covers the other long side and both short sides.
A similar one with numbers: a pen is 9 m long and 4 m wide with one long side against a wall. The fence is 9 + 4 + 4 = 17 m.

stepByStep.text: A rectangle has two long sides of p metres and two short sides of q metres.
One long side is the wall, so the fence covers one long side and two short sides.
Add them: p + q + q.
The length of the fence is (p + 2q) m.

misconceptions.A: Yes! One long side and two short sides make p + 2q.
misconceptions.B: This is the whole perimeter. The side along the wall needs no fence, so one p is left out.
misconceptions.C: Here a short side was left out. It is a long side, p metres, that lies along the wall.
misconceptions.D: This is only one long side and one short side. The fence runs along three sides.

G4A_ALGEBRA_007.questionText: If a = 6 and b = 4, what is the value of 3a − 2b + ab?
hints: Put the numbers in place of the letters. Two letters written side by side, or a number next to a letter, mean multiply.
Work out each part on its own: 3a means 3 times 6, 2b means 2 times 4, and ab means 6 times 4.
A similar one: if a = 2 and b = 5, then 4a − b + ab is 8 − 5 + 10 = 13.

stepByStep.text: 3a means 3 times a.
2b means 2 times b.
ab means a times b.
Put the parts together.
The value is 34.

misconceptions.A: 74 comes from reading ab as the number 64. Letters side by side mean multiply, so ab is 6 times 4.
misconceptions.B: 20 comes from reading ab as a + b. Letters side by side mean multiply, so ab is 24.
misconceptions.C: 50 comes from adding 2b. The sign in front of 2b is minus.

G4A_ALGEBRA_008.questionText: The nth odd number is 2n − 1 and the nth even number is 2n. How much more is the 30th odd number than the 12th even number?
hints: Use each rule to find the actual number first. Then subtract the smaller from the greater.
For the 30th odd number put n = 30 into 2n − 1. For the 12th even number put n = 12 into 2n.
A similar one: the 10th odd number is 2 times 10, minus 1, which is 19. The 6th even number is 12. The difference is 19 − 12 = 7.

stepByStep.text: The 30th odd number: put n = 30 into 2n − 1.
The 12th even number: put n = 12 into 2n.
Subtract.
The 30th odd number is 35 more.

misconceptions.A: 18 is 30 − 12, the difference of the positions. Find the two numbers themselves first.
misconceptions.B: 36 comes from using 60 as the 30th odd number. Odd numbers are one less than 2n, so it is 59.
misconceptions.D: 37 comes from using 61, which adds 1 instead of taking 1 away. The 30th odd number is 59.

G4A_ALGEBRA_009.questionText: Anu is x years old. Her father's age is 4 years more than three times Anu's age. What will be the sum of their ages after 5 years?
hints: Write each person's age now as an expression. After some years, every person is older by that many years.
Three times Anu's age is 3x, so her father is 3x + 4 now. In 5 years, both of them will be 5 years older.
A similar one: Ravi is y years old and his mother is 20 more than twice his age, which is 2y + 20. After 3 years they are y + 3 and 2y + 23, and the sum is 3y + 26.

stepByStep.text: Father's age now: three times x and 4 more, which is 3x + 4.
After 5 years Anu is x + 5 and her father is 3x + 4 + 5 = 3x + 9.
Add: x + 5 + 3x + 9. The x terms make 4x and the numbers make 14.
The sum of their ages will be 4x + 14.

misconceptions.A: 4x + 9 adds 5 years for only one person. Both Anu and her father grow 5 years older.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Now the sum is 4x + 4, and two people each gain 5 years, giving 4x + 14.
misconceptions.C: 4x + 4 is the sum of their ages now. After 5 years each of them is 5 years older.
misconceptions.D: 3x + 14 leaves out Anu's own age x. Add her age to her father's 3x.

G4A_ALGEBRA_010.questionText: Three numbers come one after another. The smallest of them is n. What is the sum of the three numbers?
hints: Numbers that come one after another go up by 1 each time. Write all three numbers using n before adding.
The smallest is n. The next is n + 1. Write the third number, then add the three expressions.
A similar one: two numbers one after another, the smaller being k, are k and k + 1. Their sum is 2k + 1. Check with 7 and 8: the sum is 15.

stepByStep.text: The three numbers are n, n + 1 and n + 2.
Add them: n + n + 1 + n + 2.
The n terms make 3n and the numbers make 1 + 2 = 3.
The sum is 3n + 3.

misconceptions.A: Yes! n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3. Try 4, 5, 6: the sum is 15.
misconceptions.B: 3n would be right if all three numbers were n. The next two are 1 more and 2 more.
misconceptions.C: n + 3 counts n only once. Each of the three numbers has an n in it.
misconceptions.D: 3n + 2 uses n + 1 for both the second and third numbers. The third number is n + 2.

G4A_ALGEBRA_011.questionText: A taxi charges ₹50 for the first kilometre and ₹12 for every kilometre after that. Which expression gives the fare, in rupees, for a ride of d kilometres (d is more than 1)?
hints: Split the ride into two parts: the first kilometre, and all the kilometres after it. Count carefully how many kilometres come after the first.
After the first kilometre there are d − 1 kilometres left. Each of those costs ₹12. Add the ₹50 for the first kilometre.
A similar one: an auto charges ₹30 for the first kilometre and ₹10 for each one after. For k kilometres the fare is 30 + 10(k − 1) = 30 + 10k − 10 = 10k + 20.

stepByStep.text: The first kilometre costs ₹50.
The remaining kilometres number d − 1, and each costs ₹12, so they cost 12(d − 1) = 12d − 12.
Add the two parts: 50 + 12d − 12.
The fare is 12d + 38.

misconceptions.A: 12d + 50 charges ₹12 for all d kilometres and ₹50 as well. The first kilometre is paid for only once, at ₹50.
misconceptions.B: 62d charges ₹50 and ₹12 for every kilometre. The ₹50 is only for the first kilometre.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 50 + 12(d − 1) = 12d + 38. For 2 km that gives ₹62, which is 50 + 12.
misconceptions.D: 12d + 62 counts one kilometre too many at ₹12. Only d − 1 kilometres come after the first.

G4A_ALGEBRA_012.questionText: Riya has 3 boxes with m mangoes in each and 5 loose mangoes. Sameer has 2 boxes with m mangoes in each and 4 loose mangoes. Riya gives one full box to Sameer. How many more mangoes does Sameer have than Riya now?
hints: Write an expression for each child's mangoes after the box has moved. Then subtract Riya's expression from Sameer's.
After giving a box, Riya has 2 boxes and 5 loose mangoes. Sameer now has 3 boxes and 4 loose mangoes.
A similar one: Asha has 4 bags of k marbles and 2 loose, Bela has 3 bags of k and 6 loose. Asha gives Bela a bag. Now Asha has 3k + 2 and Bela has 4k + 6, so Bela has k + 4 more.

stepByStep.text: After giving one box, Riya has 2 boxes and 5 loose mangoes: 2m + 5.
Sameer now has 3 boxes and 4 loose mangoes: 3m + 4.
Subtract Riya's from Sameer's. The boxes give 3m − 2m = m, and the loose mangoes give 4 − 5, which takes 1 away.
Sameer has m − 1 more mangoes.

misconceptions.A: m + 9 adds the loose mangoes together. To compare, subtract: Sameer has 4 loose and Riya has 5.
misconceptions.B: 5m + 9 is all the mangoes the two children have together. The question asks how many more Sameer has.
misconceptions.C: 1 compares only the loose mangoes. Sameer now has one more box than Riya too.

G4A_ALGEBRA_013.questionText: The letter n stands for an even number. Which expression gives the 5th odd number that comes after n?
hints: Try the idea with a small even number of your own and list the odd numbers that follow it.
The first odd number after the even number n is n + 1. Write the next ones from there.
Similar problem: the 3rd odd number after the even number 20. The odd numbers after 20 are 21, 23, 25, so the 3rd is 25, which is 20 + 5.

stepByStep.text: n is even, so the very next number, n + 1, is the first odd number after it.
Odd numbers go up in twos: n + 1, n + 3, n + 5, n + 7, n + 9.
Check with n = 10: the odd numbers after 10 are 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, and 19 is 10 + 9.
The 5th odd number after n is n + 9.

misconceptions.A: This comes from 5 jumps of 2. That works when you start on an odd number, but n is even, so the first jump is only 1. List the odd numbers after 10 and see.
misconceptions.B: This counts on 5 numbers, but some of those are even. Count only the odd ones.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The first odd number is just 1 after the even number n, and four more jumps of 2 bring you to n + 9.
misconceptions.D: This skips n + 1. The first odd number after an even number is the very next number.

G4A_ALGEBRA_014.questionText: A piece of wire is bent to make a square with each side (3a + 6) cm long. The same wire is then straightened and bent to make a triangle with three equal sides. How long is each side of the triangle?
hints: The wire does not get longer or shorter. Think about what stays the same for both shapes.
First find the whole length of the wire: a square has 4 equal sides of (3a + 6) cm.
Similar problem: a wire makes a square of side (3b + 3) cm. Its length is 4 × (3b + 3) = 12b + 12 cm. Bent into a triangle with equal sides, each side is (12b + 12) ÷ 3 = (4b + 4) cm.

stepByStep.text: The wire is as long as the perimeter of the square: 4 × (3a + 6) = 12a + 24 cm.
The triangle uses the same wire, so its three equal sides add up to 12a + 24 cm.
Share it equally among 3 sides: 12a ÷ 3 = 4a and 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
Each side of the triangle is (4a + 8) cm.

misconceptions.A: Well done! The wire is 12a + 24 cm long, and sharing it among 3 equal sides gives 4a + 8 cm each.
misconceptions.B: This is the whole length of the wire. The triangle has 3 equal sides, so one more step is needed.
misconceptions.C: This multiplies the side of the square by 3. Find the length of the whole wire first, then share it among the 3 sides.
misconceptions.D: This divides one side of the square by 3. It is the whole wire, all 4 sides, that is shared among the 3 sides of the triangle.

G4A_ALGEBRA_015.questionText: If 2x + y = 10, what is the value of 6x + 3y − 4?
hints: You do not need to know x or y on their own. Look for the given expression hiding inside the new one.
Compare 6x + 3y with 2x + y. How many times bigger is each part?
Similar problem: if a + 2b = 7, find 4a + 8b + 1. Each part is 4 times bigger, so 4a + 8b = 4 × 7 = 28, and 28 + 1 = 29.

stepByStep.text: 6x is 3 times 2x, and 3y is 3 times y, so 6x + 3y is 3 times (2x + y).
Now take away 4.
The value of 6x + 3y − 4 is 26.

misconceptions.A: This multiplies 10 by 6. Only the x part has become 6x; check how many times bigger the whole of 2x + y has become.
misconceptions.B: This is the value of 6x + 3y. One small step is left: take away the 4.
misconceptions.C: This doubles 10. Compare 2x with 6x again to see how many lots of (2x + y) there are.
misconceptions.D: Great thinking! 6x + 3y is 3 lots of (2x + y), which is 30, and taking away 4 leaves 26.

G4A_ALGEBRA_016.questionText: The letter p stands for an odd number. Which of these is always a multiple of 4?
hints: The word 'always' matters. One test is not enough, so try more than one odd number in each expression.
Try p = 1 and then p = 3 in each expression and see which ones stay multiples of 4 both times.
Similar problem: q is an even number; is q + 2 always a multiple of 4? With q = 2 it is 4, but with q = 4 it is 6, so it is not always a multiple of 4.

stepByStep.text: Test p = 1: p + 3 = 4, 2p = 2, 4p + 2 = 6 and 2p + 2 = 4. Only p + 3 and 2p + 2 are still possible.
Test p = 3: p + 3 = 6, which is not a multiple of 4, but 2p + 2 = 8, which is.
Why it always happens: 2p + 2 is 2 × (p + 1). Because p is odd, p + 1 is even, and 2 times an even number is a multiple of 4.
The expression that is always a multiple of 4 is 2p + 2.

misconceptions.A: With p = 1 this gives 4, so it looks promising. Try p = 3 as well and see what happens.
misconceptions.B: Yes! 2p + 2 is 2 × (p + 1). Because p is odd, p + 1 is even, and twice an even number is always a multiple of 4.
misconceptions.C: 4p is a multiple of 4, but adding 2 moves it off the multiples of 4. Try p = 1.
misconceptions.D: Twice an odd number is even, but it is never a multiple of 4. Try p = 3.

G4A_ALGEBRA_017.questionText: Three years ago, Meena was twice as old as Ravi was then. Ravi is x years old now, and x is more than 3. How old is Meena now, in years?
hints: There are two moments in this story: three years ago and now. Keep track of which moment each age belongs to.
Start with Ravi: if he is x years old now, write his age three years ago.
Similar problem: two years ago Asha was three times as old as Bala was then, and Bala is y now. Two years ago Bala was y − 2 and Asha was 3 × (y − 2) = 3y − 6. Now Asha is 3y − 6 + 2 = 3y − 4.

stepByStep.text: Three years ago Ravi was x − 3 years old.
Then Meena was twice that: 2 × (x − 3) = 2x − 6 years old.
That was three years ago, so add 3 to reach her age now: 2x − 6 + 3.
Meena is 2x − 3 years old now.

misconceptions.A: This is Meena's age three years ago. The question asks for her age now, so move forward 3 years.
misconceptions.B: Well done! Three years ago Meena was 2x − 6, and adding the 3 years back gives 2x − 3.
misconceptions.C: This doubles Ravi's age now. The 'twice as old' was true three years ago, so start from Ravi's age then.
misconceptions.D: This adds 3 to Ravi's age. Meena was twice as old as Ravi three years ago, so find Ravi's age then and double it.

G4A_ALGEBRA_018.questionText: Rina makes a row of squares with matchsticks. The first square needs 4 matchsticks. Each new square shares one side with the square before it, so it needs only 3 more matchsticks. How many matchsticks does she need for a row of n squares?
hints: Try small rows first and count, then look for a rule that fits every row.
Count the matchsticks for 1 square, 2 squares and 3 squares: 4, 7, 10. How many squares are 'new' in a row of n squares?
Similar problem: a row of triangles where the first needs 3 sticks and each new one needs 2 more. For n triangles there are n − 1 new ones, so the sticks are 3 + 2 × (n − 1) = 2n + 1.

stepByStep.text: The first square uses 4 matchsticks.
In a row of n squares, the other n − 1 squares are new ones, and each needs 3 matchsticks: 3 × (n − 1) = 3n − 3.
Add them: 4 + 3n − 3 = 3n + 1.
Check with 3 squares: 3 × 3 + 1 = 10, which matches 4, 7, 10.
She needs 3n + 1 matchsticks.

misconceptions.A: This adds 3 for all n squares after the first 4. The first square is already counted, so only n − 1 squares are new. Check with 2 squares: is it 7 or 10?
misconceptions.B: This gives every square 4 matchsticks of its own. Squares next to each other share a side, so each new one needs only 3.
misconceptions.C: This adds 3 only once. Every new square adds 3 more matchsticks. Check with 3 squares.
misconceptions.D: Excellent! The first square uses 4 and the other n − 1 squares use 3 each, which makes 3n + 1.

G4A_ALGEBRA_019.questionText: Anu has (5k + 3) rupees and Bala has (3k + 11) rupees, where k is a whole number. For how many values of k from 1 to 10 does Anu have more money than Bala?
hints: Make a small table of both amounts for different values of k and compare them row by row.
Start with k = 1: Anu has 8 rupees and Bala has 14 rupees. Keep going and watch the gap between them.
Similar problem: Rita has 4k + 1 and Sam has 2k + 7, for k from 1 to 8. They are equal at k = 3 (13 each). Rita has more for k = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, which is 5 values.

stepByStep.text: Each time k goes up by 1, Anu gains 5 rupees and Bala gains only 3, so Anu catches up by 2 each time.
At k = 1 Anu has 8 and Bala has 14, a gap of 6. The gap closes at k = 4, when both have 23.
Equal is not more, so k = 4 does not count. Anu has more for k = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
Anu has more money for 6 values of k.

misconceptions.A: Great job! They are equal at k = 4, and Anu has more for k = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
misconceptions.B: This counts k = 4 as well. At k = 4 both have 23 rupees, and equal is not more.
misconceptions.C: This starts counting from k = 6. Check k = 5: Anu has 28 rupees and Bala has 26.
misconceptions.D: This is the value of k where the two amounts are equal. The question asks how many values of k give Anu more.

G4A_ALGEBRA_020.questionText: A rectangular card is (2a + 5) cm long and (a + 1) cm wide. A small square with each side a cm is cut out from one corner of the card. What is the perimeter of the card that is left?
hints: Imagine walking around the edge of the card after the corner is cut. Think about which edges disappear and which new edges appear.
Cutting the corner removes two pieces of edge, each a cm long. Now count the new edges the cut makes and how long they are.
Similar problem: a card 10 cm by 6 cm has a 2 cm square cut from one corner. Two 2 cm pieces of edge go and two new 2 cm edges appear, so the perimeter stays 2 × (10 + 6) = 32 cm.

stepByStep.text: Perimeter of the whole card: 2 × (2a + 5 + a + 1) = 2 × (3a + 6) = 6a + 12 cm.
Cutting the corner square takes away two pieces of the outside edge, each a cm long.
The cut makes two new edges on the inside of the corner, each a cm long, so the distance around does not change.
The perimeter of the card that is left is (6a + 12) cm.

misconceptions.A: This takes away the perimeter of the small square, 4a. Trace the new edge with your finger: the cut also makes new edges.
misconceptions.B: This takes away the two pieces of edge that were cut off. Remember the two new edges that the cut makes inside the corner.
misconceptions.C: Excellent thinking! The cut removes two edges of a cm and makes two new edges of a cm, so the distance around stays 6a + 12 cm.
misconceptions.D: This adds two new edges but forgets that two pieces of the old edge, just as long, have gone.

G4A_ALGEBRA_021.questionText: The nth term of a number pattern is 4n − 1, so the pattern begins 3, 7, 11, 15, ... Which of these numbers is a term of the pattern?
hints: Work backwards: undo what the rule does to n and see whether you land on a whole number.
The rule multiplies n by 4 and then subtracts 1. To undo it, first add 1, then see whether 4 divides the result exactly.
Similar problem: is 35 a term of 3n − 1? Add 1 to get 36, and 36 ÷ 3 = 12, a whole number, so 35 is the 12th term.

stepByStep.text: A term is 1 less than a multiple of 4, so adding 1 to a term must give a multiple of 4.
44 + 1 = 45, 45 + 1 = 46 and 46 + 1 = 47. None of these is a multiple of 4.
47 + 1 = 48, and 48 ÷ 4 = 12, a whole number.
So 47 is a term of the pattern: it is the 12th term.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 47 + 1 = 48 and 48 ÷ 4 = 12, so 47 is the 12th term.
misconceptions.B: Taking 1 away from 45 gives 44, a multiple of 4, which is tempting. But the rule already takes 1 away, so to undo it you add 1, and 46 is not a multiple of 4.
misconceptions.C: 44 is a multiple of 4, but every term is 1 less than a multiple of 4.
misconceptions.D: 46 is even, and every term of this pattern is odd. Add 1 to each number and look for a multiple of 4.

G4A_ALGEBRA_022.questionText: Sana has ₹s and Tara has ₹20 more than Sana. Tara gives ₹15 to Sana. Who has more money now, and how much more?
hints: When one person gives money to another, both amounts change. Write both new amounts before comparing.
Tara starts with s + 20 rupees. Write what each girl has after ₹15 moves from Tara to Sana.
Similar problem: Raj has ₹12 more than Dev, who has ₹d. Raj gives Dev ₹8. Raj now has d + 4 and Dev has d + 8, so Dev has ₹4 more.

stepByStep.text: At the start Sana has s rupees and Tara has s + 20 rupees.
After giving ₹15, Tara has s + 20 − 15 = s + 5 rupees.
After getting ₹15, Sana has s + 15 rupees.
s + 15 is 10 more than s + 5, so Sana has ₹10 more.

misconceptions.A: This takes 15 away from Tara's lead of 20. But the ₹15 also goes to Sana, so Sana's amount grows too. Write both new amounts.
misconceptions.B: This is the gap before any money moved. Work out what each girl has after the ₹15 changes hands.
misconceptions.C: Well done! Tara now has s + 5 and Sana has s + 15, so Sana is ₹10 ahead.
misconceptions.D: This is the amount that was given. Compare what each girl has after the gift: s + 15 and s + 5.

G4A_ALGEBRA_023.questionText: Five whole numbers come one after another, like 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. The middle number is m. Which expression is the sum of the smallest and the greatest of the five numbers?
hints: Write all five numbers using m, starting from the middle and stepping outwards on both sides.
The numbers just before and after m are m − 1 and m + 1. Go one more step each way to find the smallest and the greatest.
Similar problem: three numbers in a row with middle number k are k − 1, k and k + 1. The smallest plus the greatest is k − 1 + k + 1 = 2k.

stepByStep.text: The five numbers are m − 2, m − 1, m, m + 1 and m + 2.
The smallest is m − 2 and the greatest is m + 2.
Add them: m − 2 + m + 2. The − 2 and the + 2 cancel each other.
The sum of the smallest and the greatest is 2m.

misconceptions.A: This treats m as the smallest number. Here m is in the middle, so two of the numbers are smaller than m.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The smallest is m − 2 and the greatest is m + 2, and together they make exactly 2m.
misconceptions.C: This is the sum of all five numbers. The question asks only for the smallest and the greatest.
misconceptions.D: This would be the greatest number if m were the smallest. Start from the middle and step out both ways.

G4A_ALGEBRA_024.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is (10a + 6) cm. Its length is (3a + 2) cm. What is its breadth?
hints: The perimeter is made of two lengths and two breadths. Work backwards from the perimeter.
Half of the perimeter is one length plus one breadth. Find half of (10a + 6) first.
Similar problem: perimeter (8b + 10) cm and length (3b + 4) cm. Half the perimeter is 4b + 5. Take away the length: 4b + 5 − 3b − 4 = b + 1, so the breadth is (b + 1) cm.

stepByStep.text: One length and one breadth together make half the perimeter: half of 10a + 6 is 5a + 3.
Take the length away from this: 5a + 3 − (3a + 2).
The breadth is (2a + 1) cm.

misconceptions.A: This takes both lengths away from the perimeter. What is left is two breadths together, so halve it.
misconceptions.B: This takes only one length away from the whole perimeter. The perimeter has two lengths and two breadths.
misconceptions.C: This is half the perimeter, which is one length and one breadth together. Take the length away from it.
misconceptions.D: Well done! Half the perimeter is 5a + 3, and taking away the length 3a + 2 leaves 2a + 1.

G4A_ALGEBRA_025.questionText: A two-digit number has tens digit t and ones digit u. A second number is made by swapping the two digits. Which expression is the sum of the two numbers?
hints: A digit in the tens place is worth ten times the digit. Write each number using place value before adding.
The first number is worth 10t + u. Write the swapped number in the same way.
Similar problem: the number with tens digit 4 and ones digit 3 is 43, and swapped it is 34. In the sum, the tens are 4 + 3 = 7 and the ones are 3 + 4 = 7, so the sum is 77.

stepByStep.text: The first number is worth 10t + u.
After the swap, u is in the tens place and t is in the ones place, so the second number is worth 10u + t.
Add them: 10t + t = 11t and u + 10u = 11u.
The sum of the two numbers is 11t + 11u.

misconceptions.A: This adds the digits as if each were worth only itself. A digit in the tens place is worth ten times as much.
misconceptions.B: This adds the first number to itself. In the second number the digits have changed places.
misconceptions.C: This counts each digit only in the tens place. Each digit is in the tens place once and in the ones place once.
misconceptions.D: Excellent! The numbers are worth 10t + u and 10u + t, and together that is 11t + 11u.

G4A_ALGEBRA_026.questionText: The value of 3x + 2 is 20. What is the value of 3(x + 2)?
hints: The two expressions look alike, but the bracket changes what is multiplied by 3. Open the bracket first.
3(x + 2) means 3 times x and also 3 times 2. Write it without the bracket and compare it with 3x + 2.
Similar problem: 2y + 1 is 15. Then 2(y + 1) = 2y + 2, which is 1 more than 2y + 1, so it is 16.

stepByStep.text: Open the bracket: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6.
3x + 6 is 4 more than 3x + 2.
3x + 2 is 20, so add 4.
The value of 3(x + 2) is 24.

misconceptions.A: This treats 3(x + 2) as the same as 3x + 2. The bracket means the 2 is multiplied by 3 as well.
misconceptions.B: Great job! 3(x + 2) is 3x + 6, which is 4 more than 3x + 2, so it is 24.
misconceptions.C: This adds 3 × 2 = 6 to 20. But 20 already has a 2 inside it, so the new expression is only 4 more.
misconceptions.D: This is the value of 3x alone. Open the bracket and add what else is there.

G4A_ALGEBRA_027.questionText: A carpenter cuts a long wooden pole into n pieces. Each cut takes him 3 minutes. How many minutes does all the cutting take?
hints: Count the cuts, not the pieces. Try it with a small number of pieces.
To get 2 pieces you need 1 cut, and to get 3 pieces you need 2 cuts. How many cuts give n pieces?
Similar problem: cutting a ribbon into 5 pieces needs 4 cuts. If each cut takes 2 seconds, the cutting takes 4 × 2 = 8 seconds.

stepByStep.text: One cut makes 2 pieces and two cuts make 3 pieces, so the number of cuts is always 1 less than the number of pieces.
For n pieces he makes n − 1 cuts.
Each cut takes 3 minutes: 3 × (n − 1) = 3n − 3.
All the cutting takes 3n − 3 minutes.

misconceptions.A: This counts one cut for every piece. Try it with 2 pieces: how many cuts are needed?
misconceptions.B: This takes away 1 minute. It is one whole cut, 3 minutes, that is not needed.
misconceptions.C: Yes! n pieces need n − 1 cuts, and 3 × (n − 1) is 3n − 3.
misconceptions.D: This adds the 3 minutes only once. Every cut takes 3 minutes, so count the cuts and multiply.

G4A_ANGLES_001.questionText: Three angles lie side by side on a straight line. Two of them are 48° and 67°. What is the third angle?
hints: Angles that lie side by side on a straight line add up to a straight angle. Remember how many degrees that is.
A straight angle is 180°. Add the two angles you know, then see what is left.
A similar one: two angles of 50° and 70° on a straight line make 120° together, so the third angle is 180° − 120° = 60°.

stepByStep.text: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Add the two known angles.
Take this away from 180°.
The third angle is 65°.

misconceptions.A: 115° is the two known angles added together. Take that away from 180° to find the third.
misconceptions.C: 245° comes from using 360°. That is for angles all the way around a point. On a straight line the total is 180°.
misconceptions.D: 75° comes from a slip in the subtraction. Check it by adding: 115 + 65 = 180.

G4A_ANGLES_002.questionText: A round pizza is cut from the centre into 8 equal slices. Ria eats 3 slices. What angle at the centre do the remaining slices make together?
hints: The angles all the way around a point add up to 360°. Equal slices share this equally.
Find the angle of one slice by sharing 360° among 8 slices. Then count the slices that are left.
A similar one: a cake cut into 6 equal slices has 360° ÷ 6 = 60° in each slice. If 2 are eaten, the 4 left make 4 × 60° = 240°.

stepByStep.text: The angle at the centre of one slice.
Slices left.
Angle made by the slices left.
The remaining slices make an angle of 225°.

misconceptions.A: 135° is the angle of the 3 slices Ria ate. The question asks about the slices that are left.
misconceptions.B: 45° is the angle of one slice. Five slices are left.
misconceptions.C: Yes! Five slices of 45° each make 225°.
misconceptions.D: 315° is what is left after only one slice is eaten. Ria ate 3 slices.

G4A_ANGLES_003.questionText: Through how many degrees does the hour hand of a clock turn between 3 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. on the same day?
hints: The hour hand goes once around the clock, 360°, in 12 hours. Find how far it turns in one hour.
In one hour the hour hand turns 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. How many hours are there from 3 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.?
A similar one: from 1 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. is 2 and a half hours. The hour hand turns 30° + 30° for the two hours and 15° for the half hour, which is 75°.

stepByStep.text: The hour hand turns 30° every hour.
From 3 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. is 4 and a half hours.
Four hours give 120°, and half an hour gives half of 30°, which is 15°.
The hour hand turns through 135°.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 120° for the four hours and 15° more for the half hour make 135°.
misconceptions.B: 120° is the turn for 4 hours. The hour hand keeps moving during the extra half hour.
misconceptions.C: 270° uses 60° for each hour. The hour hand moves only 30° in an hour.
misconceptions.D: 150° is the turn for 5 full hours. The time from 3 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. is 4 and a half hours.

G4A_ANGLES_004.questionText: Arjun is facing East. He makes a three-quarter turn anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
hints: A quarter turn is 90° and takes you from one main direction to the next. Anticlockwise is the opposite way to the hands of a clock.
Starting from East, one quarter turn anticlockwise brings Arjun to North. Make two more quarter turns the same way.
A similar one: facing North, a half turn anticlockwise goes North to West to South. So that person ends up facing South.

stepByStep.text: Going anticlockwise, the directions come in the order East, North, West, South.
First quarter turn: East to North. Second quarter turn: North to West.
Third quarter turn: West to South.
Arjun is now facing South.

misconceptions.A: North is where Arjun faces after one quarter turn. He makes three quarter turns.
misconceptions.B: West is where Arjun faces after a half turn. One more quarter turn is still to come.
misconceptions.C: He would face East again only after a full turn. Three quarters is one quarter short of that.
misconceptions.D: Yes! East to North to West to South is three quarter turns anticlockwise.

G4A_ANGLES_005.questionText: A ladder leans against an upright wall on level ground. The ladder makes an angle of 58° with the ground. What angle does the ladder make with the wall?
hints: The ladder, the wall and the ground make a triangle. An upright wall meets level ground at a right angle.
One angle of the triangle is 90°, so the other two angles together make 90°. One of them is 58°.
A similar one: a ladder that makes 65° with the ground makes 90° − 65° = 25° with the wall.

stepByStep.text: The wall and the ground meet at 90°. The three angles of the triangle add up to 180°.
So the two angles at the ends of the ladder add up to 90°.
Take away the angle with the ground.
The ladder makes an angle of 32° with the wall.

misconceptions.A: 122° comes from taking 58° from 180°. The right angle between the wall and the ground uses up 90° of that.
misconceptions.B: Yes! 58° and 32° make 90° together, and the third angle is the right angle.
misconceptions.C: 42° comes from a slip in the subtraction. Check it by adding: 58 + 32 = 90.
misconceptions.D: 58° is the angle with the ground. The two angles would be equal only if each were 45°.

G4A_ANGLES_006.questionText: At 6:00 the hands of a clock make an angle of 180°. By how many degrees has the angle between the hands become smaller at 6:30?
hints: Both hands move. In half an hour the minute hand goes halfway around, and the hour hand moves a little too.
At 6:30 the minute hand points at 6. The hour hand is not at 6 any more: it is halfway between 6 and 7. How many degrees is half of one hour space?
A similar one: at 3:00 the angle is 90°. At 3:30 the minute hand is at 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4, so the angle is 90° − 15° = 75°. The angle became smaller by 15°.

stepByStep.text: At 6:30 the minute hand points exactly at 6.
The hour hand has moved halfway from 6 to 7. One hour space is 30°, so half of it is 15°.
So the angle between the hands at 6:30 is 15°.
Compare with the angle at 6:00.
The angle has become smaller by 165°.

misconceptions.A: 180° would be right if the hands were together at 6:30. The hour hand has moved on, halfway towards 7.
misconceptions.B: 150° allows a whole hour space of 30° between the hands. In half an hour the hour hand moves only half a space, 15°.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The angle goes from 180° down to 15°, which is 165° smaller.
misconceptions.D: 15° is the angle between the hands at 6:30. The question asks how much smaller it is than 180°.

G4A_ANGLES_007.questionText: The lamp of a lighthouse turns at a steady speed and makes one full turn every 40 seconds. Through how many degrees does it turn in 15 seconds?
hints: One full turn is 360°. Find how many degrees the lamp turns in one second, then in the number of seconds asked.
Share 360° equally among 40 seconds to get the turn in one second.
A similar one: a wheel makes a full turn in 20 seconds, so it turns 360° ÷ 20 = 18° each second. In 5 seconds it turns 5 × 18° = 90°.

stepByStep.text: A full turn is 360°. Find the turn in one second.
Multiply by 15 seconds.
The lamp turns through 135°.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The lamp turns 9° each second, and 15 × 9 = 135.
misconceptions.B: 150° uses 10° for each second. Share 360° among 40 seconds: it is 9° each second.
misconceptions.C: 24° comes from dividing 360° by 15. Divide by 40 first, because the full turn takes 40 seconds.
misconceptions.D: 600 comes from multiplying 15 by 40. In 15 seconds the lamp makes less than half a turn, so the result must be less than 180°.

G4A_ANGLES_008.questionText: The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. What is the angle?
hints: The complement of an angle is what must be added to make 90°. The supplement is what must be added to make 180°. You can test each choice.
The supplement is always 90° more than the complement. If the supplement is 3 times the complement, then that extra 90° is 2 times the complement.
A similar one: the supplement of an angle is 7 times its complement. Try 75°: its supplement is 105° and its complement is 15°, and 105 = 7 × 15. So that angle is 75°.
